rationale: Construction progress on the stale-configuration safety question: a five-voter in-memory harness now reproduces the underlying configuration gap on a multi-node history (a node that restarts from a snapshot whose configuration is the smaller three-voter set while its log already contains the committed re-promotion entry) and can be brought to leadership through the repository's own leadership-transfer API. Its final attribution step is not yet reliable: locally the restarted node's replication set at leadership time covered four peers, which does not match the stale voter set, so the producer that changed the node's configuration between NewRaft and runLeader must be identified before the acknowledged-write consequence can be attributed. This update therefore only sharpens the question and its discriminator; no experiment is submitted, and no measurement is recorded as evidence.

investigations.hypothesis: r.configurations.latest, commitment.setConfiguration and quorumSize() all use the recovered configuration, so a node that restarts from a snapshot recording a smaller voter set can win an election against that stale set and commit an entry with acknowledgements from fewer nodes than a majority of the configuration in force; the acknowledged entry is then absent from a leader elected by the configuration in force. A prerequisite that must be verified per measurement is that the restarted node's voter set is still the stale one at the moment it acts as leader, which requires comparing the node's live configuration with the peers it actually replicates to.
investigations.discriminator: Reproduce the multi-node history (bootstrap five voters, demote two so the configuration in force is three voters, snapshot the node under test, re-promote the two voters, commit later traffic so the node's commit-tracking store stages a commit index past that configuration entry, restart the node), then, before and after any leadership change, emit the node's live configuration and its replication peer set together so a repaired configuration cannot be mistaken for a stale one; only after the stale set is confirmed should the acknowledged write be applied and the holders compared against the quorum of the configuration in force.
